learningObjective: Explain why an NCHW → NHWC layout transformation can improve GPU convolution performance and identify the precondition for the transformation to pay off.

canonicalClaims.claim: Placing the channel dimension as the fastest-varying axis (NHWC) matches Tensor Core convolution kernel expectations, enabling coalesced loads along the channel/K axis and unlocking cuDNN's NHWC Tensor Core algorithms; NCHW forces less optimal or precomputed algorithm variants.
conditions: The workload uses FP16 / BF16 Tensor Core-capable kernels.
The channel count meets the Tensor Core alignment (typically multiples of 8 for FP16, 16 for INT8).
nonImplications: Does not imply NHWC is universally faster; very small channel counts and some CPU backends prefer NCHW.
Does not imply the tensor consumes different memory in the two layouts.

sourceMappings.locator: cuDNN conv layout / Tensor Core alignment

misconceptions.claim: NHWC uses less memory than NCHW because interleaving channels saves storage.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Layout is a permutation of the same elements; total memory is identical.

misconceptions.claim: A layout change modifies the convolution's numerical output.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Layout only affects storage order; the mathematical convolution result is invariant to layout.

misconceptions.claim: NCHW is deprecated on Ampere and later; cuDNN silently rejects it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both NCHW and NHWC are supported; cuDNN selects the appropriate algorithm and may insert layout transforms.

misconceptions.claim: NHWC is always faster than NCHW for every workload.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For very small channel counts (C=1, 3), or on some AMD / CPU backends, NCHW can be preferable.

implementationFacts: cuDNN NHWC Tensor Core algorithms include CUDNN_CONVOLUTION_FWD_ALGO_IMPLICIT_PRECOMP_GEMM and *_TENSOR_OP variants.
PyTorch supports `channels_last` memory format that maps to NHWC while keeping the NCHW logical shape.
performanceScenarios: ResNet on Ampere: switching to channels_last typically yields 1.3-1.8× speedup on Tensor-Core-capable kernels.
Layout transformations at network entry/exit incur a permutation kernel cost that must be amortized.
